title: Geometric inverse image of the sheaf naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a common universe of sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$. In module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=K_B$ be the standard two-term complex of [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison]: put $P=A[B]$, let $J=\ker(P\twoheadrightarrow B)$ for evaluation $[b]\mapsto b$, and put $K_B=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{[h]\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Apply the same construction to $u^{-1}A\to u^{-1}B$ on $\mathcal C$. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$u^{-1}\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{u^{-1}B/u^{-1}A}\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Mod}(u^{-1}B))$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where the left side is obtained by applying inverse image termwise to the displayed standard complex. The comparison is induced by the canonical identifications of the pulled-back polynomial algebra, evaluation kernel, conormal quotient and relative differential module.

proof.text: Put $F=u^{-1}$, $A'=FA$, $B'=FB$, $P'=A'[B']$ and $J'=\ker(P'\to B')$. Apply the polynomial-algebra clause of lem-trf-geometric-standard-differential-comparison with $R=A,E=B$: it gives $FP\cong P'$ and identifies $F(P\to B)$ with evaluation $P'\to B'$, since the coefficient and variable maps and the evaluation counit are preserved. Exactness of transported module inverse image identifies $FJ$ with the kernel $J'$, compatibly with its inclusion in $P'$ and with multiplication by $FP=P'$. These comparisons are of sheaf rings and modules; no surjectivity on the sections over an individual site object is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08TZ, lemma-pullback-NL, omitted polynomial-presentation comparison; cotangent.tex Tag 08SV, free/forgetful square, supplies the polynomial comparison.

proof.text: Realize $J^2\subset P$ as the image of multiplication $\mu:J\otimes_P J\to P$. The bilinear universal property constructs $\mu$ from $(x,y)\mapsto xy$. Indeed the tensor is the sheafification of sectionwise tensors; its sections locally are finite sums of pure tensors, by the local representation property of sheafification. The sheaf image of $\mu$ therefore consists exactly of sections locally finite sums of products of sections of $J$, which is the definition of $J^2$ in the standard presentation. The same calculation applies to $J'$. Under $FJ=J'$ and the canonical tensor comparison, $F\mu$ becomes $J'\otimes_{P'}J'\to P'$: the tensor comparison preserves pure tensors, and transported ring operations preserve multiplication. An exact functor preserves images, since in an abelian category $\operatorname{im}(v)=\ker(\operatorname{coker}(v))$. Hence $F(J^2)=(J')^2$ as submodules of $P'$, compatibly with the inclusions in $FJ=J'$.

proof.text: Apply exactness to the cokernel of $J^2\hookrightarrow J$. Step 2 identifies the resulting inclusion with $(J')^2\hookrightarrow J'$, so it gives the canonical isomorphism $c^{-1}:F(J/J^2)\xrightarrow{\sim}J'/(J')^2$. It is $B'$-linear: the $P$-action on $J/J^2$ factors through $P/J=B$ because every product of two elements of $J$ vanishes in that quotient; the transported action factors through the identified evaluation $P'\to B'$ and is the usual action on $J'/(J')^2$. This uses a cokernel of sheaves, and does not replace it by a possibly non-surjective map on sections.

source.place: Tag 08TZ, lemma-pullback-NL, conormal quotient in the standard two-term presentation of Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis).

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials to the ring-sheaf map $A\to P$. Its isomorphism $F\Omega_{P/A}\cong\Omega_{P'/A'}$ carries the inverse image of $\mathrm d$ to $\mathrm d'$. Apply the tensor comparison with coefficient ring $P$, modules $\Omega_{P/A}$ and $B$, and transported coefficient ring $FP=P'$. Together they give $c^0:F(\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{P'/A'}\otimes_{P'}B'$. This is $B'$-linear, since the $B$-action on the second tensor factor transports to the $B'$-action on that same factor. Its normalization is $F(\omega\otimes b)\mapsto F\omega\otimes Fb$ in the sense of generalized sections, with the differential identification on the first factor.

source.place: Tag 08TZ, lemma-pullback-NL, hint to use Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials); Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback).

proof.text: Let $q:J\to J/J^2$ and $q':J'\to J'/(J')^2$ be the quotient maps, and let $i:J\to P$, $i':J'\to P'$ be the inclusions. By the definition of the displayed standard differential, $d_Kq$ is $J\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega_{P/A}\xrightarrow{\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes1}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B$. Steps 1 and 4 identify its inverse image with the analogous composite for $J'$, because they preserve $i$, the universal derivation, pure tensors and the ring unit. Step 3 gives $c^{-1}Fq=q'$ under $FJ=J'$. Consequently $c^0F(d_K)Fq=d_{K'}c^{-1}Fq$. The map $Fq$ is an epimorphism by exactness, so cancellation gives $c^0F(d_K)=d_{K'}c^{-1}$. Thus $c^{-1},c^0$ are the two components of a canonical chain isomorphism $FK_B\cong K_{B'}$; the inverse components commute with the differentials by the same equality. Apply the localization functor defining the derived category to this actual complex isomorphism. Since $\mathrm{NL}_{B'/A'}=K_{B'}$, its image is exactly the required isomorphism. All its maps were the specified polynomial, kernel, quotient, differential and tensor comparisons.
